bug_semantics: picklescan trusted its extraction and denylist classification of pickle GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL references to decide whether a file was dangerous. A cloudpickle payload can instead serialize a reconstructed Python function: its visible globals are cloudpickle.cloudpickle helpers such as _make_function and _builtin_type, while a CodeType bytecode object implements getattr(builtins, "eval")(payload). Before the fix those reconstruction primitives were not in _unsafe_globals, so they were at most Suspicious and did not increment issues_count or infected_files. A consumer relying on that clean result could then unpickle the attacker-controlled file, reconstruct and invoke the hidden function, and execute the attacker payload on the loading host.
flaw_origin: Commit c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e first introduced the scanner and its vulnerable blacklist-only decision: scan_pickle_bytes extracted global names, looked each module up in _suspicious_globals, and incremented issues_count only for an explicit module/name match. The direct parent contained no scanner source at all. Later refactors retained the same security boundary by making unlisted imports merely Suspicious rather than Dangerous, so they did not create the bypass.
ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e` shows human author and committer Matthieu Maitre <mmaitre314@users.noreply.github.com> and the sole message `Implement Pickle scanner`; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, other AI attribution trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: The assigned first-party GHSA bundle describes the getattr(builtins, eval) cloudpickle PoC, affected range `< 1.0.1`, and first patched version 1.0.1, and links PR #59 and commit 173c8f2a869ea9b69b543477525ec70611c3c6f4. In the validated clone, `git show 87629cb05c4521d14766eea174de0e1172d8acde:src/picklescan/scanner.py` shows _list_globals collecting only GLOBAL/INST/STACK_GLOBAL references and _build_scan_result_from_raw_globals incrementing issues_count only for _unsafe_globals matches; other unlisted names become SafetyLevel.Suspicious. `git show 173c8f2a869ea9b69b543477525ec70611c3c6f4:tests/data2/cloudpickle_codeinjection.pkl` disassembled with Python pickletools exposes cloudpickle.cloudpickle _make_function, _builtin_type, _make_empty_cell, _function_setstate, _make_cell, and subimport as STACK_GLOBAL values, constructs CodeType, embeds the strings eval/getattr in function code, and finally REDUCE-invokes that function with the command string. `git show --patch 173c8f2a869ea9b69b543477525ec70611c3c6f4` directly closes that path by adding those six cloudpickle helpers and types.CodeType to _unsafe_globals and adds regression payloads/assertions. For the origin, `git log -L :scan_pickle_bytes:src/picklescan/scanner.py c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e` attributes the original explicit-match-only classification to c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e, and `git log --all --reverse -S'_suspicious_globals.get' -- src/picklescan/scanner.py` independently returns that commit first. `git ls-tree -r --name-only 6a76b8c3ac67dc04181e600614ecf2a423cca326` lists only .gitignore, LICENSE, README.md, conda.yaml, requirements.txt, and setup.cfg, directly proving the parent lacks the scanner and vulnerable decision. The BIC has one parent and is not a merge/squash aggregate. `git log --ancestry-path --reverse v1.0.0..v1.0.1` gives b0292af34a06a6f84a0433aa80f1cc589d7e101a (v1.0.0), then 87629cb05c4521d14766eea174de0e1172d8acde, direct fix 173c8f2a869ea9b69b543477525ec70611c3c6f4, and release-tip 4d9bc9cd34bca8672dad3481cd4556d5ba747156; `git tag --contains 173c8f2a869ea9b69b543477525ec70611c3c6f4 --sort=creatordate` begins at v1.0.1. GitHub's v1.0.1 release notes likewise name #59 as `Missing detection by simple obfuscation of a builtins.eval call`.
reasoning: The earliest causal change is the initial scanner implementation, not a later refactor or the 2026 fix: its security verdict was defined as explicit denylist membership, and its parent had no scanner capable of making the false-safe judgment. The advisory payload exploits exactly that inherited boundary by moving eval/getattr into reconstructed bytecode behind global names the denylist did not cover. Commit 173c8f2a869ea9b69b543477525ec70611c3c6f4 is the direct closing fix because it makes every reconstruction primitive visible in the supplied exploit dangerous and ships the corresponding regression payload/assertions; it lands after vulnerable v1.0.0 and is contained by first-patched v1.0.1. The BIC commit object has a human identity and no qualifying AI marker, so later AI status, PR metadata, and fix authorship are irrelevant and the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
